questions.text:
Consider a water tank shown in the figure. It has one wall at $x = L$ and can be taken to be very wide in the $z$ direction. When filled with a liquid of surface tension $S$ and density $\rho$, the liquid surface makes angle $\theta_0\ (\theta_0 << 1)$ with the $x$-axis at $x = L$. If $y(x)$ is the height of the surface then the equation for $y(x)$ is :
(take $\theta(x) = \sin\theta(x) = \tan\theta(x) = \dfrac{dy}{dx}$, $g$ is the acceleration due to gravity)
questions.sol:
For a gently curved surface the curvature is $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ (since $dy/dx << 1$), and the pressure difference across it is $\Delta P = S\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ (the surface is very wide in $z$, so only one curvature counts).
At height $y$ above the flat level this must balance the hydrostatic pressure difference $\rho g y$.
So $\rho g y = S\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$, i.e. $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{\rho g}{S}y$.

questions.text: A microscope has an objective of focal length 2 cm, eyepiece of focal length 4 cm and the tube length of 40 cm. If the distance of distinct vision of eye is 25 cm, the magnification in the microscope is
questions.sol: For a compound microscope (final image at infinity), $m = \dfrac{L}{f_o}\times\dfrac{D}{f_e} = \dfrac{40}{2}\times\dfrac{25}{4} = 20 \times 6.25 = 125$.

questions.text: An electron (mass $9\times10^{-31}$ kg and charge $1.6\times10^{-19}$ C) moving with speed $c/100$ ($c$ = speed of light) is injected into a magnetic field $\vec{B}$ of magnitude $9\times10^{-4}$ T perpendicular to its direction of motion. We wish to apply an uniform electric field $\vec{E}$ together with the magnetic field so that the electron does not deflect from its path. Then (speed of light $c = 3\times10^{8}\ \text{ms}^{-1}$)
options: $\vec{E}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{B}$ and its magnitude is $27\times10^{4}\ \text{V m}^{-1}$
$\vec{E}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{B}$ and its magnitude is $27\times10^{2}\ \text{V m}^{-1}$
$\vec{E}$ is parallel to $\vec{B}$ and its magnitude is $27\times10^{2}\ \text{V m}^{-1}$
$\vec{E}$ is parallel to $\vec{B}$ and its magnitude is $27\times10^{4}\ \text{V m}^{-1}$
questions.sol:
No deflection needs $q\vec{E} = -q(\vec{v}\times\vec{B})$, so $\vec{E}$ must be perpendicular to both $\vec{v}$ and $\vec{B}$, with $E = vB$.
$v = c/100 = 3\times10^{6}\ \text{ms}^{-1}$, so $E = 3\times10^{6}\times 9\times10^{-4} = 2.7\times10^{3} = 27\times10^{2}\ \text{V m}^{-1}$.

questions.text: There are two inclined surfaces of equal length ($L$) and same angle of inclination $45^\circ$ with the horizontal. One of them is rough and the other is perfectly smooth. A given body takes 2 times as much time to slide down on rough surface than on the smooth surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction $(\mu_k)$ between the object and the rough surface is close to
questions.sol:
From rest over the same length, $L = \tfrac{1}{2}at^2$, so $t \propto 1/\sqrt{a}$. $t_r = 2t_s$ gives $a_s = 4a_r$.
$g\sin45^\circ = 4(g\sin45^\circ - \mu_k g\cos45^\circ) \Rightarrow \mu_k = \tfrac{3}{4}\tan45^\circ = 0.75$.

questions.text: The kinetic energies of two similar cars A and B are 100 J and 225 J respectively. On applying breaks, car A stops after 1000 m and car B stops after 1500 m. If $F_A$ and $F_B$ are the forces applied by the breaks on cars A and B, respectively, then the ratio $F_A/F_B$ is
questions.sol:
By the work-energy theorem the braking work equals the kinetic energy lost: $F d = K$.
$F_A = 100/1000 = 0.1$ N and $F_B = 225/1500 = 0.15$ N, so $F_A/F_B = \dfrac{0.1}{0.15} = \dfrac{2}{3}$.

questions.text: The current passing through the battery in the given circuit, is:
questions.sol:
Points C and D are joined by a wire, and A and F are joined by a wire. The battery branch (1.5 $\Omega$, 5.5 $\Omega$ and $\tfrac{1}{3}\ \Omega$ in series, $\tfrac{22}{3}\ \Omega$) connects B to E.
Between B and E: arm B–A–E has 5 $\Omega$ and 3 $\Omega$; arm B–D–E has 2.5 $\Omega$ and 1.5 $\Omega$. Since $5/3 = 2.5/1.5$, the bridge is balanced and the 6 $\Omega$ resistor (A–D) carries no current.
$R_{BE} = \dfrac{8\times4}{8+4} = \dfrac{8}{3}\ \Omega$; total $R = \dfrac{8}{3} + \dfrac{22}{3} = 10\ \Omega$.
$I = 5/10 = 0.5$ A.

questions.text: A bob of heavy mass $m$ is suspended by a light string of length $l$. The bob is given a horizontal velocity $v_0$ as shown in figure. If the string gets slack at some point $P$ making an angle $\theta$ from the horizontal, the ratio of the speed $v$ of the bob at point $P$ to its initial speed $v_0$ is:
questions.sol:
At P the string just goes slack, so tension is zero and gravity's radial component gives the centripetal force: $mg\sin\theta = \dfrac{mv^2}{l} \Rightarrow v^2 = gl\sin\theta$.
P is at height $l(1+\sin\theta)$ above the lowest point. Energy: $v_0^2 = v^2 + 2gl(1+\sin\theta) = gl(2+3\sin\theta)$.
$\dfrac{v}{v_0} = \left(\dfrac{\sin\theta}{2+3\sin\theta}\right)^{1/2}$.

questions.text: The output (Y) of the given logic implementation is similar to the output of an/a _______ gate.
questions.sol:
The upper gate gives $\overline{A+B}$ (NOR) and the lower gate gives $\overline{A\cdot B}$ (NAND). The AND gate gives $Y = \overline{A+B}\cdot\overline{AB}$.
$\overline{A+B} = 1$ only when $A = B = 0$, and then $\overline{AB} = 1$ too; otherwise $Y = 0$. So $Y = \overline{A+B}$, the NOR output.

questions.text:
The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by
$E_z = 60\cos(5x + 1.5\times10^{9}t)$ V/m.
Then expression for the corresponding magnetic field is (here subscripts denote the direction of the field) :
questions.sol:
$B_0 = E_0/c = 60/(3\times10^{8}) = 2\times10^{-7}$ T, with the same phase as $E$.
The phase $5x + \omega t$ means travel along $-x$. $\vec{B}$ must be perpendicular to both $\vec{E}$ ($z$) and the direction of travel ($x$), so it lies along $y$ (and $\hat{z}\times\hat{y} = -\hat{x}$ is consistent).
So $B_y = 2\times10^{-7}\cos(5x + 1.5\times10^{9}t)$ T.

questions.text: A ball of mass 0.5 kg is dropped from a height of 40 m. The ball hits the ground and rises to a height of 10 m. The impulse imparted to the ball during its collision with the ground is (Take $g = 9.8\ m/s^2$)
questions.sol:
Speed just before impact $= \sqrt{2\times9.8\times40} = 28$ m/s (down); just after $= \sqrt{2\times9.8\times10} = 14$ m/s (up).
Impulse $= m\Delta v = 0.5\times(14 + 28) = 21$ N s.

questions.text: AB is a part of an electrical circuit (see figure). The potential difference “$V_A - V_B$”, at the instant when current i = 2 A and is increasing at a rate of 1 amp / second is:
questions.sol:
Going from A to B along the current: drop across the inductor $= L\dfrac{di}{dt} = 1\times1 = 1$ V; drop across the cell (current enters its positive terminal) $= 5$ V; drop across the resistor $= iR = 2\times2 = 4$ V.
$V_A - V_B = 1 + 5 + 4 = 10$ V.

questions.sol: Magnetic moment $m = IA = I\pi r^2$. With the same current, $m_1 : m_2 = r_1^2 : r_2^2 = 1 : 4$.

questions.text: In a certain camera, a combination of four similar thin convex lenses are arranged axially in contact. Then the power of the combination and the total magnification in comparison to the power ($p$) and magnification ($m$) for each lens will be, respectively –
questions.sol:
For thin lenses in contact the powers add: $P = p + p + p + p = 4p$.
For a combination the total magnification is the product of the individual magnifications: $m\times m\times m\times m = m^4$.

questions.text:
An oxygen cylinder of volume 30 litre has 18.20 moles of oxygen. After some oxygen is withdrawn from the cylinder, its gauge pressure drops to 11 atmospheric pressure at temperature $27^\circ$C. The mass of the oxygen withdrawn from the cylinder is nearly equal to :
[Given, $R = \dfrac{100}{12}\ J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}$, and molecular mass of $O_2$ = 32, 1 atm pressure = $1.01\times10^{5}\ N/m$]
questions.sol:
Gauge pressure 11 atm means absolute pressure $= 12$ atm $= 12.12\times10^{5}$ Pa.
Moles left $n = \dfrac{PV}{RT} = \dfrac{12.12\times10^{5}\times30\times10^{-3}}{(100/12)\times300} = \dfrac{36360}{2500} \approx 14.54$.
Moles withdrawn $= 18.20 - 14.54 = 3.66$; mass $= 3.66\times32 \approx 117$ g $\approx 0.116$ kg.

questions.text: In some appropriate units, time ($t$) and position ($x$) relation of a moving particle is given by $t = x^2 + x$. The acceleration of the particle is
questions.sol:
$\dfrac{dt}{dx} = 2x + 1$, so $v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = \dfrac{1}{2x+1}$.
$a = v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{2x+1}\times\dfrac{-2}{(2x+1)^2} = -\dfrac{2}{(2x+1)^3}$.

questions.text: To an ac power supply of 220 V at 50 Hz, a resistor of 20 $\Omega$, a capacitor of reactance 25 $\Omega$ and an inductor of reactance 45 $\Omega$ are connected in series. The corresponding current in the circuit and the phase angle between the current and the voltage is, respectively -
questions.sol:
$X_L - X_C = 45 - 25 = 20\ \Omega$, so $Z = \sqrt{20^2 + 20^2} = 20\sqrt{2} \approx 28.3\ \Omega$.
$I = 220/28.3 \approx 7.8$ A, and $\tan\phi = \dfrac{X_L - X_C}{R} = 1 \Rightarrow \phi = 45^\circ$.

questions.text: The Sun rotates around its centre once in 27 days. What will be the period of revolution if the Sun were to expand to twice its present radius without any external influence? Assume the Sun to be a sphere of uniform density.
questions.sol:
With no external torque, angular momentum $I\omega$ is conserved. For a uniform sphere $I = \tfrac{2}{5}MR^2$, so $T \propto I \propto R^2$.
Doubling $R$ multiplies $T$ by 4: $T = 4\times27 = 108$ days.

questions.text: A model for quantized motion of an electron in a uniform magnetic field $B$ states that the flux passing through the orbit of the electron is $n(h/e)$ where $n$ is an integer, $h$ is Planck's constant and $e$ is the magnitude of electron's charge. According to the model, the magnetic moment of an electron in its lowest energy state will be ($m$ is the mass of the electron)
questions.sol:
Lowest state $n = 1$: $B\pi r^2 = \dfrac{h}{e} \Rightarrow r^2 = \dfrac{h}{\pi eB}$.
In the field $r = \dfrac{mv}{eB}$, so $v = \dfrac{eBr}{m}$. Magnetic moment $\mu = IA = \dfrac{ev}{2\pi r}\pi r^2 = \dfrac{evr}{2} = \dfrac{e^2Br^2}{2m}$.
$\mu = \dfrac{e^2B}{2m}\cdot\dfrac{h}{\pi eB} = \dfrac{he}{2\pi m}$.

questions.text: Three identical heat conducting rods are connected in series as shown in the figure. The rods on the sides have thermal conductivity $2K$ while that in the middle has thermal conductivity $K$. The left end of the combination is maintained at temperature $3T$ and the right end at $T$. The rods are thermally insulated from outside. In steady state, temperature at the left junction is $T_1$ and that at the right junction is $T_2$. The ratio $T_1/T_2$ is
questions.sol:
Thermal resistance $\propto 1/K$: if each side rod has resistance $r$, the middle rod has $2r$; total $4r$.
The same heat current flows through all three, so the $2T$ temperature drop divides as $1:2:1$, i.e. $T/2$, $T$, $T/2$.
$T_1 = 3T - T/2 = 2.5T$, $T_2 = 2.5T - T = 1.5T$; $T_1/T_2 = 5/3$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
The plates of a parallel plate capacitor are separated by $d$. Two slabs of different dielectric constant $K_1$ and $K_2$ with thickness $\dfrac{3}{8}d$ and $\dfrac{d}{2}$, respectively are inserted in the capacitor. Due to this, the capacitance becomes two times larger than when there is nothing between the plates.
If $K_1 = 1.25\,K_2$, the value of $K_1$ is :
questions.sol:
$C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d - t_1 - t_2 + t_1/K_1 + t_2/K_2} = 2\dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}$, so the denominator is $d/2$.
$\dfrac{d}{8} + \dfrac{3d}{8K_1} + \dfrac{d}{2K_2} = \dfrac{d}{2}$. With $K_2 = 0.8K_1$: $\dfrac{0.375}{K_1} + \dfrac{0.625}{K_1} = \dfrac{3}{8}$.
$K_1 = 8/3 \approx 2.66$.

questions.text: Two cities X and Y are connected by a regular bus service with a bus leaving in either direction every T min. A girl is driving scooty with a speed of 60 km/h in the direction X to Y notices that a bus goes past her every 30 minutes in the direction of her motion, and every 10 minutes in the opposite direction. Choose the correct option for the period T of the bus service and the speed (assumed constant) of the buses.
questions.sol:
Buses of speed $v$ are spaced $vT$ apart. Same direction: $\dfrac{vT}{v-60} = \dfrac{1}{2}$ h; opposite direction: $\dfrac{vT}{v+60} = \dfrac{1}{6}$ h.
Dividing: $\dfrac{v+60}{v-60} = 3 \Rightarrow v = 120$ km/h. Then $vT = 30$ km, so $T = \dfrac{1}{4}$ h $= 15$ min.

questions.text:
A uniform rod of mass 20 kg and length 5 m leans against a smooth vertical wall making an angle of $60^\circ$ with it. The other end rests on a rough horizontal floor. The friction force that the floor exerts on the rod is
(take g = 10 m/s$^2$)
questions.sol:
The smooth wall gives only a horizontal reaction $N_w$, which is balanced by friction: $f = N_w$.
Torques about the foot (rod at $60^\circ$ to the wall): $N_w L\cos60^\circ = mg\dfrac{L}{2}\sin60^\circ \Rightarrow N_w = \dfrac{mg}{2}\tan60^\circ = \dfrac{200}{2}\sqrt{3}$.
$f = 100\sqrt{3}$ N.

questions.text: In an oscillating spring mass system, a spring is connected to a box filled with sand. As the box oscillates, sand leaks slowly out of the box vertically so that the average frequency $\omega(t)$ and average amplitude $A(t)$ of the system change with time $t$. Which one of the following options schematically depicts these changes correctly?
questions.sol:
$\omega = \sqrt{k/m}$, and the mass falls as sand leaks, so $\omega(t)$ rises (ever more slowly).
The leaking sand carries away its kinetic energy, so the energy $\tfrac{1}{2}kA^2$ of the system falls: averaging the loss $\tfrac{1}{2}v^2\,dm$ over a cycle gives $A \propto m^{1/4}$, so $A(t)$ decreases.
Hence graph (2): $\omega$ increasing, $A$ decreasing.

questions.text: A balloon is made of a material of surface tension $S$ and its inflation outlet (from where gas is filled in it) has small area $A$. It is filled with a gas of density $\rho$ and takes a spherical shape of radius $R$. When the gas is allowed to flow freely out of it, its radius $r$ changes from $R$ to 0 (zero) in time $T$. If the speed $v(r)$ of gas coming out of the balloon depends on $r$ as $r^a$ and $T \propto S^{\alpha}A^{\beta}\rho^{\gamma}R^{\delta}$ then
questions.sol:
Excess pressure in the balloon $\propto S/r$ drives the gas out: $\tfrac{1}{2}\rho v^2 \propto \dfrac{S}{r}$, so $v \propto \sqrt{\dfrac{S}{\rho r}}$ and $a = -\tfrac{1}{2}$.
Volume outflow: $4\pi r^2\dfrac{dr}{dt} = -Av \Rightarrow dt \propto \dfrac{1}{A}\sqrt{\dfrac{\rho}{S}}\,r^{5/2}\,dr$.
Integrating from $R$ to 0: $T \propto S^{-1/2}A^{-1}\rho^{1/2}R^{7/2}$, so $\alpha = -\tfrac{1}{2}$, $\beta = -1$, $\gamma = \tfrac{1}{2}$, $\delta = \tfrac{7}{2}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text:
Consider the diameter of a spherical object being measured with the help of a Vernier callipers. Suppose its 10 Vernier Scale Divisions (V.S.D.) are equal to its 9 Main Scale Divisions (M.S.D.). The least division in the M.S. is 0.1 cm and the zero of V.S. is at $x = 0.1$ cm when the jaws of Vernier callipers are closed.
If the main scale reading for the diameter is M = 5 cm and the number of coinciding vernier division is 8, the measured diameter after zero error correction, is
questions.sol:
Least count $= 1\text{ MSD} - 1\text{ VSD} = 0.1 - 0.09 = 0.01$ cm.
Observed reading $= 5 + 8\times0.01 = 5.08$ cm. The zero error is $+0.1$ cm, so the corrected diameter $= 5.08 - 0.1 = 4.98$ cm.

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor made of circular plates is being charged such that the surface charge density on its plates is increasing at a constant rate with time. The magnetic field arising due to displacement current is :
options: constant between the plates and zero outside the plates
non-zero everywhere with maximum at the imaginary cylindrical surface connecting peripheries of the plates
zero between the plates and non-zero outside
questions.sol:
By the Ampère–Maxwell law, at distance $r$ from the axis: for $r < R$, $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0 r}{2}\dfrac{dE}{dt}$ (grows with $r$); for $r > R$, $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 \varepsilon_0 R^2}{2r}\dfrac{dE}{dt}$ (falls as $1/r$).
So the field is non-zero (off the axis) both inside and outside, and is greatest at $r = R$, the cylindrical surface joining the edges of the plates.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: An unpolarized light beam travelling in air is incident on a medium of refractive index 1.73 at Brewster's angle. Then-
options: reflected light is completely polarized and the angle of reflection is close to $60^\circ$
reflected light is partially polarized and the angle of reflection is close to $30^\circ$
both reflected and transmitted light are perfectly polarized with angles of reflection and refraction close to $60^\circ$ and $30^\circ$, respectively.
transmitted light is completely polarized with angle of refraction close to $30^\circ$
questions.sol:
Brewster's law: $\tan i_B = \mu = 1.73 = \sqrt{3}$, so $i_B = 60^\circ$, and the angle of reflection equals $60^\circ$.
At this angle the reflected light is completely plane polarised, while the transmitted (refracted, at $30^\circ$) light is only partially polarised.

questions.text: Two identical charged conducting spheres A and B have their centres separated by a certain distance. Charge on each sphere is q and the force of repulsion between them is F. A third identical uncharged conducting sphere is brought in contact with sphere A first and then with B and finally removed from both. New force of repulsion between spheres A and B (Radii of A and B are negligible compared to the distance of separation so that for calculating force between them they can be considered as point charges) is best given as :
questions.sol:
After touching A: A and C each have $q/2$. After touching B: B and C share $q + q/2$, so each has $3q/4$.
$F' \propto \dfrac{q}{2}\cdot\dfrac{3q}{4} = \dfrac{3}{8}q^2$, so $F' = \dfrac{3F}{8}$.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A container has two chambers of volumes $V_1$ = 2 litres and $V_2$ = 3 litres separated by a partition made of a thermal insulator. The chambers contains $n_1$ = 5 and $n_2$ = 4 moles of ideal gas at pressures $p_1$ = 1 atm and $p_2$ = 2 atm, respectively. When the partition is removed, the mixture attains an equilibrium pressure of :
questions.sol:
The container is closed and does no work, so the total internal energy is conserved. For the same ideal gas $U = nC_vT = \dfrac{C_v}{R}pV$, so $pV$ totals are conserved.
$p(V_1 + V_2) = p_1V_1 + p_2V_2 \Rightarrow p = \dfrac{1\times2 + 2\times3}{5} = 1.6$ atm.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A particle of mass $m$ is moving around the origin with a constant force $F$ pulling it towards the origin. If Bohr model is used to describe its motion, the radius $r$ of the $n^{\text{th}}$ orbit and the particle's speed $v$ in the orbit depend on $n$ as
questions.sol:
$F = \dfrac{mv^2}{r}$ gives $v \propto r^{1/2}$. Bohr's condition $mvr = \dfrac{nh}{2\pi}$ gives $r^{3/2} \propto n$.
So $r \propto n^{2/3}$ and $v \propto r^{1/2} \propto n^{1/3}$.

questions.text: The radius of Martian orbit around the Sun is about 4 times the radius of the orbit of Mercury. The Martian year is 687 Earth days. Then which of the following is the length of 1 year on Mercury ?
questions.sol: Kepler's third law: $T \propto r^{3/2}$. $T_{Mercury} = \dfrac{687}{4^{3/2}} = \dfrac{687}{8} \approx 86$ days, closest to 88 earth days.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A body weighs 48 N on the surface of the earth. The gravitational force experienced by the body due to the earth at a height equal to one-third the radius of the earth from its surface is :
questions.sol: $F \propto \dfrac{1}{(R+h)^2}$. At $h = R/3$: $F = 48\times\left(\dfrac{R}{4R/3}\right)^2 = 48\times\dfrac{9}{16} = 27$ N.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.text: A wire of resistance R is cut into 8 equal pieces. From these pieces two equivalent resistances are made by adding four of these together in parallel. Then these two sets are added in series. The net effective resistance of the combination is :
questions.sol: Each piece has resistance $R/8$. Four in parallel: $\dfrac{R/8}{4} = \dfrac{R}{32}$. Two such sets in series: $\dfrac{2R}{32} = \dfrac{R}{16}$.

questions.text: De-Broglie wavelength of an electron orbiting in the $n = 2$ state of hydrogen atom is close to (Given Bohr radius = 0.052 $nm$)
questions.sol: $r_2 = n^2a_0 = 4\times0.052 = 0.208$ nm. Bohr's condition $2\pi r_n = n\lambda$ gives $\lambda = \dfrac{2\pi\times0.208}{2} \approx 0.65$ nm, closest to 0.67 nm.

questions.text: An electric dipole with dipole moment $5\times10^{-6}$ Cm is aligned with the direction of a uniform electric field of magnitude $4\times10^{5}$ N/C. The dipole is then rotated through an angle of $60^\circ$ with respect to the electric field. The change in the potential energy of the dipole is :
questions.sol: $U = -pE\cos\theta$, so $\Delta U = pE(1 - \cos60^\circ) = 5\times10^{-6}\times4\times10^{5}\times\tfrac{1}{2} = 1.0$ J.

questions.text: A constant voltage of 50 V is maintained between the points A and B of the circuit shown in the figure. The current through the branch CD of the circuit is :
questions.sol:
C and D are joined by a wire, so 1 $\Omega$ and 3 $\Omega$ are in parallel (A to CD) and 2 $\Omega$ and 4 $\Omega$ are in parallel (CD to B).
$R = \dfrac{3}{4} + \dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{25}{12}\ \Omega$, $I = 50\times\dfrac{12}{25} = 24$ A.
$V_{AC} = 24\times\dfrac{3}{4} = 18$ V, so 18 A flows in 1 $\Omega$; $V_{CB} = 32$ V, so 16 A flows in 2 $\Omega$.
Current in CD (from C to D) $= 18 - 16 = 2.0$ A.

questions.text: A photon and an electron (mass $m$) have the same energy $E$. The ratio $(\lambda_{\text{photon}}/\lambda_{\text{electron}})$ of their de Broglie wavelengths is: ($c$ is the speed of light)
questions.sol:
Photon: $\lambda_p = \dfrac{hc}{E}$. Electron: $\lambda_e = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mE}}$.
$\dfrac{\lambda_p}{\lambda_e} = \dfrac{c\sqrt{2mE}}{E} = c\sqrt{\dfrac{2m}{E}}$.

questions.text: Which of the following options represent the variation of photoelectric current with property of light shown on the x-axis?
questions.sol:
Photoelectric current is proportional to the intensity of light (above the threshold frequency), so graph A is correct and B is wrong.
For a fixed intensity, the photoelectric (saturation) current does not depend on the frequency, so graphs C and D are wrong. Hence A only.

questions.text: A sphere of radius $R$ is cut from a larger solid sphere of radius $2R$ as shown in the figure. The ratio of the moment of inertia of the smaller sphere to that of the rest part of the sphere about the Y-axis is :
questions.sol:
Let the small sphere have mass $m$; the full sphere (8 times the volume) has mass $8m$.
Small sphere (centre at distance $R$ from the Y-axis): $I_s = \tfrac{2}{5}mR^2 + mR^2 = \tfrac{7}{5}mR^2$.
Full sphere: $I = \tfrac{2}{5}(8m)(2R)^2 = \tfrac{64}{5}mR^2$, so the rest has $\tfrac{57}{5}mR^2$.
Ratio $= 7/57$.

questions.text: A full wave rectifier circuit with diodes ($D_1$) and ($D_2$) is shown in the figure. If input supply voltage $V_{in} = 220\sin(100\pi t)$ volt, then at $t$ = 15 $msec$
options: $D_1$ is forward biased, $D_2$ is reverse biased
$D_1$ is reverse biased, $D_2$ is forward biased
questions.sol:
At $t = 15$ ms, $V_{in} = 220\sin(1.5\pi) = -220$ V, so the input is in its negative half-cycle.
In this centre-tap rectifier exactly one diode conducts in each half-cycle while the other is reverse biased, so (3) and (4) are wrong.
Which diode conducts depends on the winding sense of the transformer, which the figure does not fix. The NTA final key accepts both (1) and (2).

questions.text: Two gases $A$ and $B$ are filled at the same pressure in separate cylinders with movable pistons of radius $r_A$ and $r_B$, respectively. On supplying an equal amount of heat to both the systems reversibly under constant pressure, the pistons of gas $A$ and $B$ are displaced by 16 $cm$ and 9 $cm$, respectively. If the change in their internal energy is the same, then the ratio $r_A/r_B$ is equal to
questions.sol:
$Q = \Delta U + W$ with equal $Q$ and $\Delta U$, so the work $W = p\Delta V$ is equal. With equal pressure, $\Delta V$ is equal.
$\pi r_A^2\times16 = \pi r_B^2\times9 \Rightarrow \dfrac{r_A}{r_B} = \dfrac{3}{4}$.

questions.text: The ratio of the wavelengths of the light absorbed by a Hydrogen atom when it undergoes $n = 2 \rightarrow n = 3$ and $n = 4 \rightarrow n = 6$ transitions, respectively, is
questions.sol:

questions.text:
Which of the following statements are true?
A. Unlike Ga that has a very high melting point, Cs has a very low melting point.
B. On Pauling scale, the electronegativity values of N and Cl are not the same.
C. Ar, $\mathrm{K^+}$, $\mathrm{Cl^-}$, $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}}$, and $\mathrm{S^{2-}}$ are all isoelectronic species.
D. The correct order of the first ionization enthalpies of Na, Mg, Al, and Si is Si > Al > Mg > Na.
E. The atomic radius of Cs is greater than that of Li and Rb.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A is false: gallium has a very low melting point (303 K), like caesium.
B is false: N and Cl both have electronegativity 3.0 on the Pauling scale.
C is true: all five species have 18 electrons.
D is false: the order is Si > Mg > Al > Na (Mg has a stable $3s^2$ configuration).
E is true: atomic radius increases down the group, so Cs > Rb > Li. Hence C and E only.

questions.text:
Which of the following are paramagnetic?
A. $\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$
B. $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$
C. $\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$
D. $\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$
E. $\mathrm{Ni(PPh_3)_4}$
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{[NiCl_4]^{2-}}$: Ni(II), $d^8$, weak-field $\mathrm{Cl^-}$, tetrahedral, 2 unpaired electrons – paramagnetic.
$\mathrm{[Ni(H_2O)_6]^{2+}}$: octahedral $d^8$ ($t_{2g}^6e_g^2$), 2 unpaired – paramagnetic.
$\mathrm{[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}}$ is square planar $d^8$ (all paired), and $\mathrm{Ni(CO)_4}$ and $\mathrm{Ni(PPh_3)_4}$ are Ni(0), $d^{10}$ – diamagnetic. Hence A and D only.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Like nitrogen that can form ammonia, arsenic can form arsine.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Antimony cannot form antimony pentoxide.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
All group 15 elements form hydrides $\mathrm{EH_3}$: $\mathrm{NH_3}$, $\mathrm{PH_3}$, $\mathrm{AsH_3}$ (arsine), etc., so Statement I is correct.
Antimony does form antimony pentoxide, $\mathrm{Sb_2O_5}$ (group 15 elements form $\mathrm{E_2O_3}$ and $\mathrm{E_2O_5}$), so Statement II is incorrect.

questions.text:
Which among the following electronic configurations belong to main group elements?
A. [Ne]$3s^1$
B. [Ar]$3d^34s^2$
C. [Kr]$4d^{10}5s^25p^5$
D. [Ar]$3d^{10}4s^1$
E. [Rn]$5f^06d^27s^2$
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the option given below :
questions.sol:
Main group (s- and p-block) elements have their last electron in an s or p orbital.
A (Na, s-block) and C (I, p-block) are main group elements.
B (V) and D (Cu) are d-block, and E (Th) is f-block. Hence A and C only.

questions.text: Dalton's Atomic theory could not explain which of the following?
questions.sol:
Dalton's theory explains the laws of chemical combination by mass (conservation of mass, constant proportions, multiple proportions).
It could not explain Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes, which needed Avogadro's idea of molecules.

With $t_{1/2} = 1$ min, $t \approx 10$ minutes.

questions.text:
The correct order of the wavelength of light absorbed by the following complexes is,
A. $\mathrm{[Co(NH_3)_6]^{3+}}$
B. $\mathrm{[Co(CN)_6]^{3-}}$
C. $\mathrm{[Cu(H_2O)_4]^{2+}}$
D. $\mathrm{[Ti(H_2O)_6]^{3+}}$
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A larger crystal field splitting $\Delta$ means the light absorbed has higher energy, i.e. a smaller $\lambda$ ($\Delta = hc/\lambda$).
$\mathrm{CN^-}$ is stronger than $\mathrm{NH_3}$, which is stronger than $\mathrm{H_2O}$, and $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ complexes have large $\Delta$; $\mathrm{[Cu(H_2O)_4]^{2+}}$ has the smallest $\Delta$.

questions.text: Which one of the following compounds can exist as cis-trans isomers?
questions.sol:
Cis-trans isomerism needs two different groups on each of two carbons of a double bond or ring.
Pent-1-ene has $=\mathrm{CH_2}$, 2-methylhex-2-ene has two $\mathrm{CH_3}$ on C2, and 1,1-dimethylcyclopropane has both methyls on one carbon, so none of these shows it.
In 1,2-dimethylcyclohexane the two methyls can be on the same side (cis) or opposite sides (trans) of the ring.

questions.text:
Phosphoric acid ionizes in three steps with their ionization constant values $K_{a_1}$, $K_{a_2}$ and $K_{a_3}$, respectively, while K is the overall ionization constant. Which of the following statements are true?
A. $\log K = \log K_{a_1} + \log K_{a_2} + \log K_{a_3}$
B. $\mathrm{H_3PO_4}$ is a stronger acid than $\mathrm{H_2PO_4^-}$ and $\mathrm{HPO_4^{2-}}$.
C. $K_{a_1} > K_{a_2} > K_{a_3}$
D. $K_{a_1} = \dfrac{K_{a_3} + K_{a_2}}{2}$
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
The overall constant is the product $K = K_{a_1}K_{a_2}K_{a_3}$, so A is true.
Removing a proton from a neutral molecule is easier than from an anion, so $K_{a_1} > K_{a_2} > K_{a_3}$ (C true) and $\mathrm{H_3PO_4}$ is the strongest acid of the three (B true).
D has no basis. Hence A, B and C only.

$\textbf{Statement II :}$ As bond order increases, the bond length increases.

$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Ferromagnetism is considered as an extreme form of paramagnetism.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ The number of unpaired electrons in a $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$ ion (Z = 24) is the same as that of a $\mathrm{Nd^{3+}}$ ion (Z = 60).

$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Benzenediazonium salt is prepared by the reaction of aniline with nitrous acid at 273 - 278 K. It decomposes easily in the dry state.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Insertion of iodine into the benzene ring is difficult and hence iodobenzene is prepared through the reaction of benzenediazonium salt with KI.

questions.text: How many products (including stereoisomers) are expected from monochlorination of the following compound?
questions.sol:
The compound is 2-methylbutane, with four kinds of hydrogen.
Chlorine on a $\mathrm{CH_3}$ of the isopropyl end gives 1-chloro-2-methylbutane (chiral: 2 enantiomers); on C2 gives 2-chloro-2-methylbutane (1); on C3 gives 2-chloro-3-methylbutane (chiral: 2); on C4 gives 1-chloro-3-methylbutane (1).
Total $= 2 + 1 + 2 + 1 = 6$.

questions.text: Among the given compounds I-III, the correct order of bond dissociation energy of C–H bond marked with * is :
questions.sol:
More s-character in the carbon orbital gives a shorter, stronger C–H bond: $sp$ (II, alkyne C–H) > $sp^2$ (I, aryl C–H).
In III the marked C–H is on an $sp^3$ carbon, and breaking it gives a resonance-stabilised (allylic-type) radical, so its bond is the weakest.
Order: II > I > III.

questions.text: Which one of the following compounds $\underline{\textbf{does not}}$ decolourize bromine water?
questions.sol:
Phenol and aniline have strongly activated rings and react with bromine water at once (giving 2,4,6-tribromo products), and styrene adds bromine across its C=C bond, so all three decolourise it.
Cyclohexane is a saturated alkane and does not react with bromine water, so option (1).

questions.text: The major product of the following reaction is :
questions.sol:
Excess $\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}$ adds to both groups. The ketone C=O gives a tertiary alkoxide, which on hydrolysis becomes a tertiary alcohol (Ph, $\mathrm{CH_3}$ and OH on one carbon).
The nitrile adds one $\mathrm{CH_3MgBr}$ to give an imine salt, which $\mathrm{H_3O^+}$ hydrolyses to a methyl ketone ($-\mathrm{COCH_3}$).
So the product is option (2).

questions.text: Which of the following aqueous solution will exhibit highest boiling point?
questions.sol:
Elevation of boiling point $\propto iC$ (effective particle concentration).
Urea: $1\times0.01 = 0.01$; $\mathrm{KNO_3}$: $2\times0.01 = 0.02$; $\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}$: $3\times0.01 = 0.03$; glucose: $1\times0.015 = 0.015$.
$\mathrm{Na_2SO_4}$ has the highest boiling point.

questions.text: 5 moles of liquid X and 10 moles of liquid Y make a solution having a vapour pressure of 70 torr. The vapour pressures of pure X and Y are 63 torr and 78 torr respectively. Which of the following is true regarding the described solution?
options: The solution has volume greater than the sum of individual volumes.
questions.sol:
For an ideal solution, by Raoult's law: $p = \tfrac{5}{15}\times63 + \tfrac{10}{15}\times78 = 21 + 52 = 73$ torr.
The observed 70 torr is lower than 73 torr, so the solution shows negative deviation (and its volume would be less, not greater, than the sum).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion (A)}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason (R)}$.
$\textbf{Assertion (A) :}$ shown in the figure below.
$\textbf{Reason (R) :}$ Iodine is a better leaving group because of its large size.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both $\textbf{A}$ and $\textbf{R}$ are true and $\textbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\textbf{A}$
Both $\textbf{A}$ and $\textbf{R}$ are true but $\textbf{R}$ is $\textbf{not}$ the correct explanation of $\textbf{A}$
questions.sol:
In an $\mathrm{S_N2}$ reaction the C–X bond breaks in the rate-determining step. The C–I bond is longer and weaker than C–Cl, and the large iodide ion is a weak base that holds the negative charge well, so it is a better leaving group.
Hence the alkyl iodide reacts faster than the alkyl chloride: A is true and R correctly explains it.

questions.text:
The standard heat of formation, in kcal/mol of $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}$ is :
[Given : standard heat of formation of $\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}$ ion (aq) = – 216 kcal/mol, standard heat of crystallisation of $\mathrm{BaSO_4}$(s) = – 4.5 kcal/mol, standard heat of formation of $\mathrm{BaSO_4}$(s) = – 349 kcal/mol]
questions.sol:
$\mathrm{Ba^{2+}(aq) + SO_4^{2-}(aq) \rightarrow BaSO_4(s)}$, $\Delta H = -4.5$ kcal/mol (crystallisation).
$\Delta_f H(\mathrm{BaSO_4}) = \Delta_f H(\mathrm{Ba^{2+}}) + \Delta_f H(\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}}) + \Delta H_{cryst}$
$-349 = x - 216 - 4.5 \Rightarrow x = -128.5$ kcal/mol.

questions.text: Total number of possible isomers (both structural as well as stereoisomers) of cyclic ethers of molecular formula $\mathrm{C_4H_8O}$ is :
questions.sol:
Five-membered ring: oxolane (tetrahydrofuran) – 1.
Four-membered ring: 2-methyloxetane (chiral, 2) and 3-methyloxetane (1).
Three-membered ring: 2-ethyloxirane (chiral, 2), 2,2-dimethyloxirane (1) and 2,3-dimethyloxirane (cis meso form 1 + trans pair 2 = 3).
Total $= 1 + 3 + 6 = 10$.

questions.text:
Identify the correct orders against the property mentioned
A. $\mathrm{H_2O > NH_3 > CHCl_3}$ – dipole moment
B. $\mathrm{XeF_4 > XeO_3 > XeF_2}$ – number of lone pairs on central atom
C. O–H > C–H > N–O – bond length
D. $\mathrm{N_2 > O_2 > H_2}$ – bond enthalpy
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A: dipole moments are $\mathrm{H_2O}$ 1.85 D > $\mathrm{NH_3}$ 1.47 D > $\mathrm{CHCl_3}$ about 1.0 D – correct.
B: lone pairs on Xe are $\mathrm{XeF_2}$ 3, $\mathrm{XeF_4}$ 2, $\mathrm{XeO_3}$ 1, so the order given is wrong.
C: the O–H bond (about 96 pm) is shorter than C–H (about 109 pm) – wrong.
D: bond enthalpies $\mathrm{N_2}$ 946 > $\mathrm{O_2}$ 498 > $\mathrm{H_2}$ 436 kJ mol$^{-1}$ – correct. Hence A, D only.

questions.text:
Higher yield of NO in $\mathrm{N_2(g) + O_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2NO(g)}$ can be obtained at
[$\Delta H$ of the reaction = + 180.7 kJ mol$^{-1}$]
A. higher temperature
B. lower temperature
C. higher concentration of $\mathrm{N_2}$
D. higher concentration of $\mathrm{O_2}$
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
The forward reaction is endothermic, so by Le Chatelier's principle a higher temperature favours NO (A, not B).
Adding either reactant, $\mathrm{N_2}$ or $\mathrm{O_2}$, shifts the equilibrium forward (C and D). Hence A, C, D only.

questions.text:
If the rate constant of a reaction is 0.03 s$^{-1}$, how much time does it take for 7.2 mol L$^{-1}$ concentration of the reactant to get reduced to 0.9 mol L$^{-1}$?
(Given: log 2 = 0.301)
questions.sol:
The unit s$^{-1}$ shows a first order reaction, so $t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{0.03} = 23.1$ s.
$7.2 \rightarrow 3.6 \rightarrow 1.8 \rightarrow 0.9$ is three half-lives: $t = 3\times23.1 = 69.3$ s.

questions.text: Which one of the following reactions does $\textbf{NOT}$ belong to “Lassaigne's test”?
questions.sol:
In Lassaigne's test the organic compound is fused with sodium, converting N, S and halogens into NaCN, $\mathrm{Na_2S}$ and NaX.
Heating with copper(II) oxide, which oxidises carbon to $\mathrm{CO_2}$, is the test for carbon (and hydrogen), not part of Lassaigne's test.

questions.text:
What are the potential drawbacks in adoption of the IVF method?
A. High fatality risk to mother
B. Expensive instruments and reagents
C. Husband/wife necessary for being donors
D. Less adoption of orphans
E. Not available in India
F. Possibility that the early embryo does not survive
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: A, B, C, E, F only
questions.sol:
IVF needs expensive equipment and reagents (B), may discourage the adoption of orphans (D), and the early embryo may fail to survive after transfer (F).
It carries no high fatality risk to the mother (A), donors need not be the husband or wife (C), and it is available in India (E). Hence B, D, F only.

questions.text: What is the name of the blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart in a frog ?
questions.sol: In the frog, the venae cavae bring deoxygenated blood from the body to the sinus venosus and right atrium. The aorta carries blood away from the heart, the pulmonary artery carries blood to the lungs and the pulmonary vein returns oxygenated blood from the lungs.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements refers to Reductionist Biology?
options: Physico-chemical approach to study and understand living organisms.
Physiological approach to study and understand living organisms.
Chemical approach to study and understand living organisms.
Behavioural approach to study and understand living organisms.
questions.sol: Describing biological processes in terms of the physical and chemical principles underlying them is the physico-chemical approach; this is called reductionist biology.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ In the RNA world, RNA is considered the first genetic material evolved to carry out essential life processes. RNA acts as a genetic material and also as a catalyst for some important biochemical reactions in living systems. Being reactive, RNA is unstable.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ DNA evolved from RNA and is a more stable genetic material. Its double helical strands being complementary, resist changes by evolving repairing mechanism.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Both statements follow NCERT's account of the RNA world: RNA was the first genetic material and also acts as a catalyst, but its reactivity makes it unstable.
DNA evolved from RNA with chemical changes (deoxyribose, thymine) that make it more stable, and its complementary double strands allow repair. Both statements are correct.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Epiphytes that are growing on a mango branch is an example of which of the following?
questions.sol: An epiphyte (e.g. an orchid) on a mango branch gets support and access to light, while the mango tree is neither harmed nor helped. One species benefits and the other is unaffected: commensalism.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
From the statements given below choose the $\textbf{correct}$ option :
A. The eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S and prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S.
B. Each ribosome has two sub-units.
C. The two sub-units of 80S ribosome are 60S and 40S while that of 70S are 50S and 30S.
D. The two sub-units of 80S ribosome are 60S and 20S and that of 70S are 50S and 20S.
E. The two sub-units of 80S are 60S and 30S and that of 70S are 50S and 30S.
questions.sol:
Eukaryotic (cytoplasmic) ribosomes are 80S and prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S, and each has a large and a small sub-unit.
80S = 60S + 40S and 70S = 50S + 30S (S values are not additive). So A, B and C are true; D and E give wrong sub-units.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which one of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation?
questions.sol: Ex-situ ('off-site') conservation protects species outside their natural habitat, as in zoos, botanical gardens, wildlife safari parks and seed banks. National parks, wildlife sanctuaries and other protected areas conserve species in their habitats (in-situ).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ The primary source of energy in an ecosystem is solar energy.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis in an ecosystem is called net primary productivity (NPP).
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.sol:
The Sun is the only source of energy for (almost) all ecosystems, so Statement I is correct.
The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis is gross primary productivity (GPP); NPP is GPP minus respiration losses, so Statement II is incorrect.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List - I}$ with $\textbf{List - II}$.
List - IList - II
A.EmphysemaI.Rapid spasms in muscle due to low $\mathrm{Ca^{++}}$ in body fluid
B.Angina PectorisII.Damaged alveolar walls and decreased respiratory surface
C.Glomerulo-nephritisIII.Acute chest pain when not enough oxygen is reaching to heart muscle
D.TetanyIV.Inflammation of glomeruli of kidney
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Emphysema: damaged alveolar walls, so the respiratory surface decreases. Angina pectoris: acute chest pain when too little oxygen reaches the heart muscle. Glomerulonephritis: inflammation of the glomeruli. Tetany: rapid muscle spasms due to low $\mathrm{Ca^{++}}$.
So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion (A)}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason (R).}$
$\textbf{Assertion (A) :}$ Both wind and water pollinated flowers are not very colourful and do not produce nectar.
$\textbf{Reason (R) :}$ The flowers produce enormous amount of pollen grains in wind and water pollinated flowers.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both $\textbf{A}$ and $\textbf{R}$ are true and $\textbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\textbf{A}$
Both $\textbf{A}$ and $\textbf{R}$ are true but $\textbf{R}$ is $\textbf{NOT}$ the correct explanation of $\textbf{A}$
questions.sol:
Both statements are true. Wind and water pollinated flowers lack bright colours and nectar because they do not need to attract animal pollinators.
They produce huge numbers of pollen grains to make up for the heavy loss of pollen in transfer. That is a separate feature, not the reason for the lack of colour and nectar, so R does not explain A.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of non-distilled alcoholic beverage produced by yeast?
questions.sol: Wine and beer are produced by yeast fermentation without distillation, while whisky, brandy and rum are made by distilling the fermented broth.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ In a floral formula $\oplus$ stands for zygomorphic nature of the flower, and $\underline{\mathrm{G}}$ stands for inferior ovary.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ In a floral formula $\oplus$ stands for actinomorphic nature of the flower and $\underline{\mathrm{G}}$ stands for superior ovary.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
In a floral formula $\oplus$ means actinomorphic (zygomorphic is shown by %), and $\underline{\mathrm{G}}$ (line below G) means a superior ovary, while a line above G means an inferior ovary.
So Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct.

questions.sol: Streptokinase, produced by the bacterium $\textit{Streptococcus}$ and modified by genetic engineering, is used as a 'clot buster' to remove clots from the blood vessels of patients who have had a heart attack.

questions.text: Which chromosome in the human genome has the highest number of genes?
questions.sol: The Human Genome Project found that chromosome 1 has the most genes (2968), while the Y chromosome has the fewest (231).

options: First and Second digit of fore limb
First digit of the fore limb
questions.sol: Male frogs have a copulatory (nuptial) pad on the first digit of each fore limb, which helps them grip the female during amplexus. Females lack it.

questions.text: Which one of the following phytohormones promotes nutrient mobilization which helps in the delay of leaf senescence in plants?
questions.sol: Cytokinins promote nutrient mobilisation, which helps to delay leaf senescence. Ethylene and abscisic acid promote senescence.

questions.text: While trying to find out the characteristic of a newly found animal, a researcher did the histology of adult animal and observed a cavity with presence of mesodermal tissue towards the body wall but no mesodermal tissue was observed towards the alimentary canal. What could be the possible coelome of that animal ?
questions.sol: In pseudocoelomates the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm all round: mesoderm is present as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and endoderm, i.e. on the body wall side but not around the gut. A true coelom (e.g. schizocoel) is lined by mesoderm on both sides; acoelomates have no cavity.

Match $\textbf{List - I}$ with $\textbf{List - II}$.

A.HeadI.Enzymes
B.Middle pieceII.Sperm motility
C.AcrosomeIII.Energy
D.TailIV.Genetic material
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
The sperm head contains the haploid nucleus (genetic material); the middle piece has mitochondria that supply energy; the acrosome holds enzymes that help in fertilisation; the tail gives motility.

questions.text:
Given below are the stages in the life cycle of pteridophytes. Arrange the following stages in the correct sequence.
A. Prothallus stage
B. Meiosis in spore mother cells
C. Fertilisation
D. Formation of archegonia and antheridia in gametophyte.
E. Transfer of antherozoids to the archegonia in presence of water.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Spore mother cells in the sporangia undergo meiosis to form spores (B); a spore germinates into the prothallus (A); the prothallus bears antheridia and archegonia (D); antherozoids reach the archegonia through water (E); fertilisation follows (C).
Sequence: B, A, D, E, C.

questions.text:
Cardiac activities of the heart are regulated by :
A. Nodal tissue
B. A special neural centre in the medulla oblongata
C. Adrenal medullary hormones
D. Adrenal cortical hormones
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: The heart is auto-regulated by its nodal tissue (SA and AV nodes), and its activity can be moderated by a special neural centre in the medulla oblongata through the autonomic nervous system, and by adrenal medullary hormones (adrenaline, noradrenaline). Adrenal cortical hormones do not regulate cardiac activity. Hence A, B and C only.

questions.text:
Which of following organisms $\textit{cannot}$ fix nitrogen?
A. $\textit{Azotobacter}$
B. $\textit{Oscillatoria}$
C. $\textit{Anabaena}$
D. $\textit{Volvox}$
E. $\textit{Nostoc}$
Choose the $\textit{\textbf{correct}}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
$\textit{Azotobacter}$ is a free-living nitrogen-fixing bacterium, and $\textit{Oscillatoria}$, $\textit{Anabaena}$ and $\textit{Nostoc}$ are cyanobacteria that fix nitrogen.
$\textit{Volvox}$ is a green alga (a eukaryote) and cannot fix nitrogen. Hence D only.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Transfer RNAs and ribosomal RNA do not interact with mRNA.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ RNA interference (RNAi) takes place in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defence.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
During translation tRNA anticodons pair with mRNA codons and the ribosomal RNA binds the mRNA, so Statement I is incorrect.
RNA interference takes place in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defence (silencing of a specific mRNA by complementary dsRNA), so Statement II is correct.

questions.text: In the above represented plasmid an alien piece of DNA is inserted at EcoRI site. Which of the following strategies will be chosen to select the recombinant colonies?
options: Using ampicillin & tetracyclin containing medium plate.
Blue color colonies will be selected.
White color colonies will be selected.
Blue color colonies grown on ampicillin plates can be selected.
questions.sol:
The EcoRI site lies within the $\beta$-galactosidase gene. Inserting foreign DNA there inactivates the gene (insertional inactivation).
On a medium with a chromogenic substrate, recombinant colonies cannot make $\beta$-galactosidase and stay white, while non-recombinants give blue colonies. So white colonies are selected (the amp and tet genes stay intact in both kinds).

questions.text: Which of the following genetically engineered organisms was used by Eli Lilly to prepare human insulin?
questions.sol: In 1983 Eli Lilly prepared two DNA sequences for the A and B chains of human insulin and introduced them into plasmids of the bacterium $\textit{E. coli}$, which produced the insulin chains.

questions.text: Find the statement that is $\textbf{NOT}$ correct with regard to the structure of monocot stem.
options: Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed.

questions.text:
The correct sequence of events in the life cycle of bryophytes is
A. Fusion of antherozoid with egg.
B. Attachment of gametophyte to substratum.
C. Reduction division to produce haploid spores.
D. Formation of sporophyte.
E. Release of antherozoids into water.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
The dominant gametophyte is attached to the substratum by rhizoids (B); antherozoids are released into water (E) and fuse with the egg (A); the zygote forms the sporophyte (D), in which spore mother cells undergo reduction division to produce haploid spores (C).
Sequence: B, E, A, D, C.

questions.text:
Which are correct:
A. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging detect cancers of internal organs.
B. Chemotherapeutics drugs are used to kill non-cancerous cells.
C. $\alpha$-interferon activate the cancer patients' immune system and helps in destroying the tumour.
D. Chemotherapeutic drugs are biological response modifiers.
E. In the case of leukaemia blood cell counts are decreased.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
A is correct: CT and MRI detect cancers of internal organs. C is correct: $\alpha$-interferon is a biological response modifier that activates the immune system against the tumour.
B is wrong (chemotherapeutic drugs kill cancer cells), D is wrong (biological response modifiers are substances such as $\alpha$-interferon, not chemotherapeutic drugs), and E is wrong (blood cell counts increase in leukaemia). Hence A and C only.

questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List - I}$ with $\textbf{List - II}$.
List - IList - II
A.CentromereI.Mitochondrion
B.CiliumII.Cell division
C.CristaeIII.Cell movement
D.Cell membraneIV.Phospholipid Bilayer
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :

The centromere holds sister chromatids and bears kinetochores for spindle attachment in cell division; cilia bring about cell movement; cristae are infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane; the cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer.
So A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

Match $\textbf{List I}$ with $\textbf{List II}$ :
List IList II
A.Chlorophyll aI.Yellow-green
B.Chlorophyll bII.Yellow

In paper chromatography of leaf pigments: chlorophyll a is bright or blue-green, chlorophyll b is yellow-green, xanthophylls are yellow and carotenoids are yellow to yellow-orange.
So A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

questions.text:
Find the correct statements :
A. In human pregnancy, the major organ systems are formed at the end of 12 weeks.
B. In human pregnancy the major organ systems are formed at the end of 8 weeks.
C. In human pregnancy heart is formed after one month of gestation.
D. In human pregnancy, limbs and digits develop by the end of second month.
E. In human pregnancy the appearance of hair is usually observed in the fifth month.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: B, C, D and E Only
A, C, D and E Only
questions.sol:
After one month of pregnancy the embryo's heart is formed (C); by the end of the second month limbs and digits develop (D); by the end of 12 weeks (first trimester) most major organ systems are formed (A, so B is wrong); in the fifth month the first movements are felt and hair appears on the head (E).
Hence A, C, D and E only.

questions.text: In the seeds of cereals, the outer covering of endosperm separates the embryo by a protein-rich layer called :

questions.text: Which of the following diagrams is correct with regard to the proximal (P) and distal (D) tubule of the Nephron.

The proximal convoluted tubule reabsorbs $\mathrm{HCO_3^-}$, NaCl and water, and secretes $\mathrm{H^+}$ and $\mathrm{NH_3}$ into the filtrate.
The distal convoluted tubule conditionally reabsorbs NaCl, water and $\mathrm{HCO_3^-}$, and secretes $\mathrm{K^+}$ and $\mathrm{H^+}$.

questions.text: Identify the part of a bio-reactor which is used as a foam braker from the given figure.
questions.sol:
In a simple stirred-tank bioreactor the motor sits on top (B), the foam braker is the paddle just below the lid at the top of the culture (C), flat-bladed impellers stir the medium (A), and the sterile air sparger is at the bottom (D).
So the foam braker is C, option (4).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion (A)}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason (R).}$
$\textbf{Assertion (A) :}$ A typical unfertilised, angiosperm embryo sac at maturity is 8 nucleate and 7-celled.
$\textbf{Reason (R) :}$ The egg apparatus has 2 polar nuclei.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both $\textbf{A}$ and $\textbf{R}$ are true and $\textbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\textbf{A}$
Both $\textbf{A}$ and $\textbf{R}$ are true but $\textbf{R}$ is $\textbf{NOT}$ the correct explanation of $\textbf{A}$
questions.sol:
A typical mature embryo sac is 8-nucleate and 7-celled (3 antipodals, 2 synergids, 1 egg and a central cell with 2 polar nuclei), so A is true.
The egg apparatus consists of the egg cell and two synergids; the 2 polar nuclei are in the central cell, so R is false.

questions.text: A specialised membranous structure in a prokaryotic cell which helps in cell wall formation, DNA replication and respiration is :
questions.sol: Mesosomes are infoldings of the plasma membrane in prokaryotes that help in cell wall formation, DNA replication and its distribution to daughter cells, respiration and secretion. Chromatophores hold pigments; cristae and ER are found in eukaryotic cells.

questions.text:
Which of the following are the post-transcriptional events in an eukaryotic cell?
A. Transport of pre-mRNA to cytoplasm prior to splicing.
B. Removal of introns and joining of exons.
C. Addition of methyl group at 5' end of hnRNA.
D. Addition of adenine residues at 3' end of hnRNA.
E. Base pairing of two complementary RNAs.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
The hnRNA is processed in the nucleus: splicing removes introns and joins exons (B), capping adds methyl guanosine triphosphate at the 5' end (C), and tailing adds adenylate residues at the 3' end (D).
Pre-mRNA is not sent to the cytoplasm before splicing (A), and base pairing of complementary RNAs is not a processing step (E). Hence B, C, D only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: What is the pattern of inheritance for polygenic trait?
questions.sol: Polygenic traits such as human skin colour are controlled by several genes with additive effects and show continuous variation. They do not give the clear Mendelian ratios, so they follow a non-Mendelian pattern of inheritance.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which one of the following enzymes contains ‘Haem’ as the prosthetic group?
questions.sol: Peroxidase and catalase have haem as the prosthetic group; they break down hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen. Carbonic anhydrase contains zinc, and succinate dehydrogenase has FAD.

questions.text:
Each of the following characteristics represent a Kingdom proposed by Whittaker. Arrange the following in increasing order of complexity of body organization.
A. Multicellular heterotrophs with cell wall made of chitin.
B. Heterotrophs with tissue/organ/organ system level of body organization.
C. Prokaryotes with cell wall made of polysaccharides and amino acids.
D. Eukaryotic autotrophs with tissue/organ level of body organization.
E. Eukaryotes with cellular body organization.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :

C is Monera (prokaryotes; peptidoglycan wall), E is Protista (unicellular eukaryotes), A is Fungi (chitin wall), D is Plantae (tissue/organ level) and B is Animalia (tissue/organ/organ system level).
Increasing complexity: C, E, A, D, B.

questions.text: Who is known as the father of Ecology in India?
questions.sol: Professor Ramdeo Misra is revered as the father of ecology in India; he set up the first teaching and research programme in ecology at Banaras Hindu University.
