questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List I}$ with $\textbf{List II}$ :
List-IList-II
A.Alfred Hershey and Martha ChaseI.Streptococcus pneumoniae
B.EuchromatinII.Densely packed and dark-stained
C.Frederick GriffithIII.Loosely packed and light-stained
D.HeterochromatinIV.DNA as genetic material confirmation
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Hershey and Chase gave unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material; euchromatin is loosely packed and stains light; Griffith worked with $\textit{Streptococcus pneumoniae}$ (transformation); heterochromatin is densely packed and stains dark.
So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Neoplastic characteristics of cells refer to :
A. A mass of proliferating cell
B. Rapid growth of cells
C. Invasion and damage to the surrounding tissue
D. Those confined to original location
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
Malignant tumours are masses of proliferating cells, called neoplastic or tumour cells, which grow very rapidly and invade and damage the surrounding normal tissues.
Staying confined to the original location is a feature of benign tumours. Hence A, B, C only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ The DNA fragments extracted from gel electrophoresis can be used in construction of recombinant DNA.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Smaller size DNA fragments are observed near anode while larger fragments are found near the wells in an agarose gel.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Separated DNA bands are cut out of the agarose gel and extracted (elution); the purified fragments are used to construct recombinant DNA, so Statement I is correct.
DNA is negatively charged and moves towards the anode; smaller fragments move farther, so they lie near the anode while larger fragments stay near the wells. Statement II is correct.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List I}$ with $\textbf{List II}$.
List IList II
A.AdenosineI.Nitrogen base
B.Adenylic acidII.Nucleotide
C.AdenineIII.Nucleoside
D.AlanineIV.Amino acid
Choose the option with all $\textbf{correct}$ matches.
questions.sol:
Adenosine (adenine + sugar) is a nucleoside; adenylic acid (adenosine + phosphate) is a nucleotide; adenine is a nitrogen base; alanine is an amino acid.
So A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Consider the following :
A. The reductive division for the human female gametogenesis starts earlier than that of the male gametogenesis.
B. The gap between the first meiotic division and the second meiotic division is much shorter for males compared to females.
C. The first polar body is associated with the formation of the primary oocyte.
D. Luteinizing Hormone (LH) surge leads to disintegration of the endometrium and onset of menstrual bleeding.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
A is true: primary oocytes enter meiosis I in the foetal ovary, whereas spermatogenesis begins at puberty. B is true: in males meiosis II follows meiosis I quickly, while a secondary oocyte stays arrested until ovulation and fertilisation.
C is false: the first polar body forms with the secondary oocyte. D is false: the LH surge causes ovulation; menstruation follows the fall in progesterone. Hence A and B.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: All living members of the class Cyclostomata are:
questions.sol: All living members of the class Cyclostomata (lampreys and hagfishes) are ectoparasites on some fishes, which they attach to with a sucking, circular mouth.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion (A)}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason (R)}$.
$\textbf{Assertion (A) :}$ The primary function of the Golgi apparatus is to package the materials made by the endoplasmic reticulum and deliver it to intracellular targets and outside the cell.
$\textbf{Reason (R) :}$ Vesicles containing materials made by the endoplasmic reticulum fuse with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus, and they are modified and released from the trans face of the Golgi apparatus.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both $\textbf{A}$ and $\textbf{R}$ are true and $\textbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\textbf{A}$
Both $\textbf{A}$ and $\textbf{R}$ are true but $\textbf{R}$ is $\textbf{not}$ the correct explanation of $\textbf{A}$
questions.sol:
The Golgi apparatus mainly packages materials made by the ER for delivery to intracellular targets or secretion, so A is true.
ER vesicles fuse with the cis (forming) face; the materials are modified as they pass through and leave from the trans (maturing) face. This route is how the packaging is done, so R is true and explains A.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List I}$ with $\textbf{List II}$ :
List IList II
A.ScutellumI.Persistent nucellus
B.Non-albuminous seedII.Cotyledon of Monocot seed
C.EpiblastIII.Groundnut
D.PerispermIV.Rudimentary cotyledon
Choose the option with all $\textbf{correct}$ matches.
questions.sol:
The scutellum is the single cotyledon of the grass (monocot) embryo; groundnut seeds are non-albuminous (no residual endosperm); the epiblast is a rudimentary cotyledon in some grasses; perisperm is persistent nucellus (e.g. black pepper, beet).
So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion (A)}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason (R)}$.
$\textbf{Assertion (A) :}$ All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrate.
$\textbf{Reason (R) :}$ The members of subphylum vertebrata possess notochord during the embryonic period, the notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in adults.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both $\textbf{A}$ and $\textbf{R}$ are true and $\textbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\textbf{A}$
Both $\textbf{A}$ and $\textbf{R}$ are true but $\textbf{R}$ is $\textbf{not}$ the correct explanation of $\textbf{A}$
questions.sol:
Vertebrates have a notochord in the embryo, so they are chordates; but in vertebrates it is replaced by a vertebral column in the adult, which urochordates and cephalochordates never develop.
So all vertebrates are chordates but not all chordates are vertebrates: both are true and R explains A (as stated in NCERT).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Identify the statement that is $\textbf{NOT}$ correct.
options: Each antibody has two light and two heavy chains.
The heavy and light chains are held together by disulfide bonds.
Antigen binding site is located at C-terminal region of antibody molecules.
Constant region of heavy and light chains are located at C-terminus of antibody molecules.
questions.sol:
An antibody ($\mathrm{H_2L_2}$) has two heavy and two light chains held together by disulphide bonds. The variable regions, which form the antigen binding sites, are at the N-terminal ends, while the constant regions are at the C-terminal ends.
So statement (3) is not correct.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Silencing of specific mRNA is possible via RNAi because of -
questions.sol: In RNA interference a complementary double-stranded RNA binds to the specific mRNA and prevents its translation, silencing the gene.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Genes R and Y follow independent assortment. If RRYY produce round yellow seeds and rryy produce wrinkled green seeds, what will be the phenotypic ratio of the F2 generation?
questions.sol: The F1 (RrYy) is a dihybrid. With independent assortment, selfing gives round yellow : round green : wrinkled yellow : wrinkled green $= 9 : 3 : 3 : 1$ in the F2.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Histones are enriched with -
questions.sol: Histones are positively charged, basic proteins rich in the basic amino acid residues lysine and arginine, whose side chains carry positive charges that bind the negatively charged DNA.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: The first menstruation is called :
questions.sol: The first menstruation, which begins at puberty, is called menarche. Menopause is the cessation of menstruation at about 50 years.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List - I}$ with $\textbf{List - II}$.
List - IList - II
A.HeartI.Erythropoietin
B.KidneyII.Aldosterone
C.Gastro-intestinal tractIII.Atrial natriuretic factor
D.Adrenal CortexIV.Secretin
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
The atrial wall of the heart secretes atrial natriuretic factor; the juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney secrete erythropoietin; the gastro-intestinal tract secretes secretin (among others); the adrenal cortex secretes aldosterone.
So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: The protein portion of an enzyme is called :
questions.sol: In a holoenzyme the protein portion is the apoenzyme; the non-protein part is the cofactor, which may be a prosthetic group, a coenzyme or a metal ion.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following is the unit of productivity of an Ecosystem?
questions.sol: Productivity is the rate of biomass production, expressed per unit area per unit time, e.g. g $\mathrm{m^{-2}\,yr^{-1}}$ or (kcal $\mathrm{m^{-2}}$) $\mathrm{yr^{-1}}$. The other options have no time term.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Sweet potato and potato represent a certain type of evolution. Select the correct combination of terms to explain the evolution.
questions.sol: Sweet potato is a modified root and potato is a modified stem; both store food but have different origins. They are analogous organs, the result of convergent evolution.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: With the help of given pedigree, find out the probability for the birth of a child having no disease and being a carrier (has the disease mutation in one allele of the gene) in $\mathrm{F_3}$ generation.
questions.sol:
Carrier females and affected males point to an X-linked recessive trait. The $\mathrm{F_2}$ cross is a carrier female ($\mathrm{X^AX^a}$) $\times$ an affected male ($\mathrm{X^aY}$).
Children: $\mathrm{X^AX^a}$ (carrier daughter), $\mathrm{X^aX^a}$ (affected daughter), $\mathrm{X^AY}$ (normal son), $\mathrm{X^aY}$ (affected son), each with probability 1/4.
The probability of an unaffected carrier child is 1/4.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as $\textbf{Assertion (A)}$ and the other is labelled as $\textbf{Reason (R).}$
$\textbf{Assertion (A) :}$ Cells of the tapetum possess dense cytoplasm and generally have more than one nucleus.
$\textbf{Reason (R) :}$ Presence of more than one nucleus in the tapetum increases the efficiency of nourishing the developing microspore mother cells.
In light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both $\textbf{A}$ and $\textbf{R}$ are true and $\textbf{R}$ is the correct explanation of $\textbf{A}$
Both $\textbf{A}$ and $\textbf{R}$ are true but $\textbf{R}$ is $\textbf{NOT}$ the correct explanation of $\textbf{A}$
questions.sol:
The tapetum is the innermost wall layer of the microsporangium; its cells have dense cytoplasm and generally more than one nucleus, so A is true.
The tapetum nourishes the developing pollen, and being multinucleate with dense cytoplasm makes it metabolically very active, which increases its nourishing efficiency. The final key treats R as true and as the correct explanation of A.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: How many meiotic and mitotic divisions need to occur for the development of a mature female gametophyte from the megaspore mother cell in an angiosperm plant?
questions.sol:
The megaspore mother cell undergoes one meiosis to form four megaspores. The functional megaspore's nucleus then divides mitotically three times (giving 2, 4 and then 8 nuclei) to form the 8-nucleate embryo sac.
So 1 meiosis and 3 mitoses.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a zygomorphic flower?
questions.sol: A zygomorphic flower can be divided into two similar halves in only one vertical plane, as in pea, gulmohur, bean and Cassia. Petunia, Datura and chilli (Solanaceae) have actinomorphic flowers.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
After maturation, in primary lymphoid organs, the lymphocytes migrate for interaction with antigens to secondary lymphoid organ(s) / tissue(s) like:
A. thymus
B. bone marrow
C. spleen
D. lymph nodes
E. Peyer's patches
Choose the $\textit{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
The bone marrow and thymus are primary lymphoid organs, where lymphocytes form and mature.
The spleen, lymph nodes, tonsils, Peyer's patches of the small intestine and appendix are secondary lymphoid organs, where lymphocytes meet antigens. Hence C, D, E only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ Fig fruit is a non-vegetarian fruit as it has enclosed fig wasps in it.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Fig wasp and fig tree exhibit mutual relationship as fig wasp completes its life cycle in fig fruit and fig fruit gets pollinated by fig wasp.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Statement I is incorrect: the fig is a plant product; any wasp remains inside are broken down by the fig's enzymes, so it is not a non-vegetarian fruit.
Statement II is incorrect as worded: in this mutualism the wasp pollinates the fig $\textit{inflorescence}$ (its flowers) while looking for egg-laying sites; a fruit is not pollinated. The NTA final key marks both statements incorrect.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: What is the main function of the spindle fibers during mitosis ?
questions.sol: Spindle fibres attach to the kinetochores of chromosomes and, at anaphase, pull the sister chromatids apart to opposite poles, separating the chromosomes. DNA is synthesised in S phase, not by the spindle.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which one of the following is the characteristic feature of gymnosperms?
questions.sol: Gymnosperms ('naked seeds') have ovules that are not enclosed by an ovary wall, so the seeds remain exposed before and after fertilisation. They have no flowers or fruits.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Consider the following statements regarding function of adrenal medullary hormones :
A. It causes pupilary constriction
B. It is a hyperglycemic hormone
C. It causes piloerection
D. It increases strength of heart contraction
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Adrenaline and noradrenaline (emergency hormones) cause pupillary dilation (not constriction), piloerection, sweating, a faster heartbeat with stronger contraction and a higher breathing rate. They also stimulate glycogenolysis, raising blood glucose (hyperglycaemic).
Hence B, C and D only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Why can't insulin be given orally to diabetic patients?
options: Human body will elicit strong immune response
It will be digested in Gastro-Intestinal (GI) tract
questions.sol: Insulin is a polypeptide hormone. Taken by mouth it would be digested by proteolytic enzymes in the gastro-intestinal tract before it could be absorbed, so it is given by injection.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List I}$ with $\textbf{List II}$.
List IList II
A.PteridophyteI.$\textit{Salvia}$
B.BryophyteII.$\textit{Ginkgo}$
C.AngiospermIII.$\textit{Polytrichum}$
D.GymnospermIV.$\textit{Salvinia}$
Choose the option with all $\textbf{correct}$ matches.
questions.sol:
$\textit{Salvinia}$ is a pteridophyte (water fern), $\textit{Polytrichum}$ is a moss (bryophyte), $\textit{Salvia}$ is an angiosperm and $\textit{Ginkgo}$ is a gymnosperm.
So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Who proposed that the genetic code for amino acids should be made up of three nucleotides?
questions.sol: The physicist George Gamow argued that since there are 20 amino acids and only 4 bases, the code must be made of three nucleotides ($4^3 = 64$ combinations).
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List I}$ with $\textbf{List II}$ :
List IList II
A.The Evil QuartetI.Cryopreservation
B.Ex situ conservationII.Alien species invasion
C.$\textit{Lantana camara}$III.Causes of biodiversity losses
D.DodoIV.Extinction
Choose the option with all correct matches.
questions.sol:
The 'Evil Quartet' names the four major causes of biodiversity loss; cryopreservation of gametes is an ex situ method; $\textit{Lantana camara}$ is an invasive alien weed; the dodo (Mauritius) is an extinct bird.
So A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following hormones released from the pituitary is actually synthesized in the hypothalamus ?
questions.sol: Oxytocin and vasopressin (ADH) are synthesised by hypothalamic neurons and carried along their axons to the posterior pituitary (neurohypophysis), from which they are released. LH, FSH and ACTH are made in the anterior pituitary.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Role of the water vascular system in Echinoderms is :
A. Respiration and Locomotion
B. Excretion and Locomotion
C. Capture and transport of food
D. Digestion and Respiration
E. Digestion and Excretion
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol: The water vascular system of echinoderms helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration. It has no role in digestion or excretion. Hence A and C only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following type of immunity is present at the time of birth and is a non-specific type of defence in the human body?
questions.sol: Innate immunity is non-specific defence present from birth, provided by barriers such as skin, mucus, phagocytes and interferons. Acquired immunity (humoral and cell-mediated) is pathogen-specific and develops after exposure.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: In bryophytes, the gemmae help in which one of the following?
questions.sol: Gemmae are green, multicellular, asexual buds formed in gemma cups on liverwort thalli (e.g. $\textit{Marchantia}$). They detach and grow into new plants, so they help in asexual reproduction.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: In frog, the Renal portal system is a special venous connection that acts to link :
options: Kidney and lower part of body
questions.sol: Frogs have a hepatic portal system (between the intestine and liver) and a renal portal system, a special venous connection between the kidney and the lower parts of the body.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Given below are two statements :
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ In ecosystem, there is unidirectional flow of energy of sun from producers to consumers.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ Ecosystems are exempted from 2$^{\text{nd}}$ law of thermodynamics.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
questions.sol:
Energy flows in one direction, from the Sun to producers and then to consumers, so Statement I is correct.
Ecosystems are not exempt from the second law of thermodynamics; they need a constant supply of energy to make up for the energy lost as heat, so Statement II is incorrect.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which of the following statements about RuBisCO is true?
options: It is active only in the dark.
It has higher affinity for oxygen than carbon dioxide.
It is an enzyme involved in the photolysis of water.
It catalyzes the carboxylation of RuBP.
questions.sol: RuBisCO (RuBP carboxylase-oxygenase) catalyses the carboxylation of RuBP in the Calvin cycle. It has a higher affinity for $\mathrm{CO_2}$ than for $\mathrm{O_2}$, works in the light-driven Calvin cycle, and plays no part in the photolysis of water.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Which of the following enzyme(s) are $\textbf{NOT}$ essential for gene cloning?
A. Restriction enzymes
B. DNA ligase
C. DNA mutase
D. DNA recombinase
E. DNA polymerase
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Gene cloning needs restriction enzymes to cut DNA, DNA ligase to join the fragments and DNA polymerase (for example in PCR) to amplify the gene.
'DNA mutase' and 'DNA recombinase' are not among the essential tools, so C and D only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Read the following statements on plant growth and development.
A. Parthenocarpy can be induced by auxins.
B. Plant growth regulators can be involved in promotion as well as inhibition of growth.
C. Dedifferentiation is a pre-requisite for re-differentiation.
D. Abscisic acid is a plant growth promoter.
E. Apical dominance promotes the growth of lateral buds.
Choose the option with all correct statements.
questions.sol:
A, B and C are correct: auxins induce parthenocarpy (e.g. in tomato), PGRs can promote or inhibit growth, and cells must dedifferentiate before they redifferentiate.
D is wrong (ABA is a growth inhibitor) and E is wrong (apical dominance suppresses lateral buds). Hence A, B, C only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which factor is important for termination of transcription?
questions.sol: In bacteria the RNA polymerase associates with the initiation factor $\sigma$ to start transcription and with the termination factor $\rho$ (rho) to end it.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Frogs respire in water by skin and buccal cavity and on land by skin, buccal cavity and lungs.
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the following :
options: The statement is true for water but false for land
The statement is true for both the environment
The statement is false for water but true for land
The statement is false for both the environment
questions.sol:
In water a frog respires through its skin only (cutaneous respiration, by diffusion). On land the buccal cavity, skin and lungs are all respiratory organs.
So the statement is false for water but true for land.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Twins are born to a family that lives next door to you. The twins are a boy and a girl. Which of the following must be true?
options: They were conceived through in vitro fertilization.
questions.sol: Monozygotic (identical) twins come from one zygote and are always of the same sex. Twins of different sex must come from two separately fertilised eggs, so they are fraternal (dizygotic) twins, sharing on average about 50% of their genes like ordinary siblings.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Which of the following microbes is $\textbf{NOT}$ involved in the preparation of household products?
A. $\textit{Aspergillus niger}$
B. $\textit{Lactobacillus}$
C. $\textit{Trichoderma polysporum}$
D. $\textit{Saccharomyces cerevisiae}$
E. $\textit{Propionibacterium sharmanii}$
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below:
questions.sol:
$\textit{Lactobacillus}$ (curd), $\textit{Saccharomyces cerevisiae}$ (bread) and $\textit{Propionibacterium sharmanii}$ (Swiss cheese) are used for household products.
$\textit{Aspergillus niger}$ is used industrially for citric acid, and $\textit{Trichoderma polysporum}$ produces the immunosuppressant cyclosporin A. Hence A and C only.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
Match $\textbf{List - I}$ with $\textbf{List - II}$.
List - IList - II
A.ProgesteroneI.Pars intermedia
B.RelaxinII.Ovary
C.Melanocyte stimulating hormoneIII.Adrenal Medulla
D.CatecholaminesIV.Corpus luteum
Choose the $\textbf{correct}$ answer from the options given below :
questions.sol:
Progesterone is secreted mainly by the corpus luteum; relaxin by the ovary (in later pregnancy); MSH by the pars intermedia of the pituitary; catecholamines (adrenaline, noradrenaline) by the adrenal medulla.
So A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text:
The blue and white selectable markers have been developed which differentiate recombinant colonies from non-recombinant colonies on the basis of their ability to produce colour in the presence of a chromogenic substrate.
Given below are two statements about this method:
$\textbf{Statement I :}$ The blue coloured colonies have DNA insert in the plasmid and they are identified as recombinant colonies.
$\textbf{Statement II :}$ The colonies without blue colour have DNA insert in the plasmid and are identified as recombinant colonies.
In the light of the above statements, choose the $\textbf{most appropriate}$ answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.sol:
The insert goes into the $\beta$-galactosidase coding region and inactivates it (insertional inactivation).
Non-recombinant colonies still make the enzyme and turn blue with the chromogenic substrate; recombinant colonies stay colourless (white). So Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct.
questions.subject: Biology

questions.text: Which one of the following equations represents the Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth of population?
questions.sol: Logistic growth: $\dfrac{dN}{dt} = rN\left(\dfrac{K-N}{K}\right)$, where $N$ is the population density, $r$ the intrinsic rate of natural increase and $K$ the carrying capacity. Growth slows as $N$ approaches $K$.
questions.subject: Biology
